routes.description: Establish Christian theism through a cumulative inference from cosmic origin and order, biological complexity, mind-independent logic and mathematics, objective moral obligation, human purpose, religious experience, and the character of Jesus.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the relevant features of reality are better explained by a transcendent personal mind than by atheistic naturalism, and connect that mind to the Christian conception of God strongly enough to establish the motion.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative inference to the existence of the personal God asserted by Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Establish that cosmic origin, physical intelligibility, fine-tuning, or biological information materially support an intelligent source.
Establish that mind-independent logic, mathematics, reason, and moral obligation require or favor a transcendent personal ground.
Provide a warranted step from a transcendent source to the Christian God through Jesus, the cross, or distinctively Christian claims.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why theistic grounding accounts for altruism, human value, purpose, and flourishing better than the proposed naturalistic accounts.
Specify how personal experience may support commitment while allowing that divine reasons can exceed human knowledge.

routes.description: Defeat the inference to God by enforcing the claimant's evidential burden, defending methodological naturalism, supplying non-theistic accounts of the disputed phenomena, and challenging Christian revelation and religious experience.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the pro considerations neither require nor reliably identify a deity, that available naturalistic explanations block the asserted inferences, and that faith, revelation, and experience do not provide independently verifiable grounds for the motion.

motionBridge.description: Connect the unmet evidential burden and defeated identification inferences to nonestablishment of the asserted God's existence.

centralBridges.description: Require the party asserting God to provide testable or independently verifiable support beyond faith and unsupported supernatural addition.
Show that evolution, constrained natural processes, social morality, and finite human meaning do not require divine causation.
Show that conflicting experiences, religious diversity, scriptural problems, and Christian doctrines undermine reliable identification of the proposed God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test design claims against inefficient biological complexity, evolutionary mechanisms, and the explanatory limits of invoking supernatural agency.
Explain why absent reliable divine disclosure supports warranted nonbelief rather than shifting responsibility to the skeptic.

sections.title: Evidence, Burden, and Methodological Naturalism
sections.rationale: The debate turns first on what evidence an existence claim requires, whether faith or personal certainty can supply knowledge, and whether supernatural explanation adds testable information.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Physical Order, and Design
sections.rationale: Claims about the universe's beginning, comprehensibility, physical laws, fine-tuning, and constrained natural processes form a distinct clash over whether cosmic features warrant an originating mind.

sections.title: Biological Complexity, Evolution, and Intelligent Design
sections.rationale: Cellular information, irreducible complexity, evolutionary accumulation, inefficient mechanisms, and endosymbiosis bear directly on whether living systems support intelligent design.

sections.title: Logic, Mathematics, and Rational Order
sections.rationale: The status of mind-independent logical and mathematical truths tests whether immaterial rational order requires a transcendent mind or remains true without divine grounding.

sections.title: Morality, Human Value, Purpose, and Altruism
sections.rationale: Objective obligation, human worth, costly assistance, social cooperation, finite meaning, and flourishing comprise the central dispute over what theism and naturalism can ground.

sections.title: Christian Revelation, Religious Experience, and Hiddenness
sections.rationale: Jesus, the cross, scripture, conflicting religious experiences, religious diversity, and absent public verification determine whether a general theistic inference can be identified with Christianity.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: The universe's comprehensibility and governing physical laws support an inference to an intelligent designer.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The information-rich complexity and nanotechnology evident in living cells are unexpected on materialism and indicate a designer.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Enduring mathematical laws are more intelligible as products of a personal creative mind than as human inventions or unexplained abstractions.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Mind-independent laws of logic constitute an immaterial rational order that is grounded in God's nature and enables communication and science.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Objective human value and genuine moral obligation require a mind beyond humanity rather than value assigned solely by individuals.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Increasing knowledge of cellular complexity and internal machinery supports a teleological inference to intelligent design.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Christian theism should be assessed through the historical character of Jesus and the cross as divine self-sacrifice rather than as worship of a merely coercive ruler.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Evidence can establish the reliability of Christian theism, while personal experience supplies the certainty involved in committed belief.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Biological evolution does not explain cosmic origins, and ordinary causal reasoning makes an originating mind behind the universe plausible.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-001.proposition: Serving God promotes human flourishing, while loving service to other people supplies a purpose under which the world functions at its best.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-007.proposition: A God great enough to be blamed for hiddenness may possess reasons for nondisclosure that human beings do not know.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Faith cannot establish that God exists or identify a particular god because incompatible religious convictions lack physical, logical, and testable verification.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Methodological naturalism preserves inquiry into real causes, whereas invoking an unobservable God supplies neither a mechanism nor testable explanatory information.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Morality arises through social trust, empathy, cooperation, and disfavor toward harmful selfishness rather than requiring the Christian God.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Concern for humanity and society, together with the intrinsic satisfaction of materially helping others, can motivate secular altruism without divine reward.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Biological complexity is better explained by haphazard cumulative development than intelligent design because evolved mechanisms can be unnecessarily convoluted and inefficient.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Christian scripture, biblical history, souls, and an afterlife provide no reliable basis for inferring that the Christian God exists.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Mathematical relations would remain equally true in an otherwise equivalent universe without God, so their validity does not require a divine mind.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Conflicting near-death experiences across religions undermine supernatural experience as reliable evidence for the distinctively Christian conception of God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: A universe without a divine plan need not be wholly random because natural processes constrain probabilities and guide outcomes without predetermination.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Intelligent design repackages creationism and relies on irreducible-complexity claims whose alleged barriers to evolutionary explanation have failed.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Atheism need not assert creation from nothing because the earliest cosmos remains uncertain and live cosmological models can treat an initial singularity as eternal.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-002.proposition: If accumulated knowledge disappeared, empirical inquiry would rediscover the same natural facts, whereas historically inherited religions would emerge differently.
